paper.title_en: Specific heat in the BCS-rashbon BEC crossover regime of an ultracold Fermi gas with a 3D spherical spin-orbit coupling
paper.abstract_en: We theoretically investigate strong-coupling properties of an ultracold Fermi gas with a tunable spherical (isotropic) spin-orbit interaction. In this spin-orbit coupled system, it is known that a two-body bound state, called rashbon, can be formed even in the coupling regime where a pairing interaction alone cannot form such a two-body bound molecule. In this paper, we evaluate the specific heat at constant volume $C_V$, including pairing fluctuations in the presence of SOC within the framework of the strong-coupling theory developed by Nozières and Schmitt-Rink, to show that this thermodynamic quantity is very useful to see how system properties vary from a Fermi gas to a rashbon gas with increasing spin-orbit coupling strength. At the superfluid phase transition temperature $T_{\rm c}$, $C_V$ is found to exhibit a peak structure in the intermediate spin-orbit coupling regime between the weak-coupling Fermi gas regime and a strong-SOC rashbon gas regime. In the normal state above $T_{\rm c}$, from detailed analyses of the temperature dependences of $C_V$, we also identify the regions where system properties are dominated by (1) a Fermi atomic gas, (2) a Bose gas of stable rashbons, and (3) fluctuating rashbons. Combining these results with the conventional Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS)--Bose-Einstein condensation (BEC) crossover physics realized by tuning the strength of a pairing interaction, we present a unified description of the BCS--BEC and BCS--rashbon BEC crossover phenomena.
